subject: Post-call: cost runway, batching options & approval path
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Post-call: cost runway, batching options & approval path

Katie / Luke — thanks again for your time today. Short recap below plus recommended next steps so we can get the pilot moving without surprises.

TL;DR
- Primary pain: token spend volatility on NLU scoring during peak-clearing windows and inconsistent latency when handling concurrent batch scoring jobs.
- Goal agreed: reduce per-request inference cost by ~30–40% while keeping 95th pctl latency under 200ms for the scoring path.
- Proposed pilot: 4 weeks (2-week bench + 2-week controlled load) to validate unit economics and ops runbook.

What we heard (pain & constraints)
1) Budget: SummitPay has a firm Q3 token budget cap (~$120k) for the feature launch window. No open-ended spend.
2) Latency: customer-facing scoring must be <200ms P95 to avoid UX regressions. Batch reconciliation can tolerate higher latencies.
3) Ops: limited SRE time to integrate custom caching — prefer plug-and-play routing and managed KV cache where possible.
4) Procurement: contract review + finance sign-off needed before any paid pilot; timeline target: decision within 10 business days.

Levers we recommended (cost & performance)
- Batching: continuous batching for reconciliation jobs to reduce per-token cost; target 2–3x effective throughput improvement in batch window.
- KV/prefix caching: apply to stable prefixes (merchant metadata) to cut repeated token generation.
- Model variant routing: serve latency-sensitive scoring on a low-latency quantized variant; route lower-priority traffic to cheaper variants.
- Dedicated pool vs hosted: show comparative TCO in pilot; dedicated may lower unit cost if commit levels are met.

Pilot scope (proposed)
1) Week 0–1: access & instrumentation — sandbox keys, data samples, latency/cost baseline capture.
2) Week 2: implement batching + KV cache in test harness; run synthetic profiles.
3) Week 3: controlled live traffic (shadow/percentage) to measure unit economics and latency.
4) Week 4: readout & recommendation (TCO delta, suggested commit level).

Deliverables we will share
- Filled cost model (attached: summitpay_cost_model_v1.xlsx)
- Pilot statement (attached: redwood_pilot_statement.pdf)
- Runbook for routing & fallback behavior

Immediate asks for SummitPay
- Confirm pilot approvers (finance/procurement contact + technical owner) and any required PO process.
- Provide representative sample traces (anonymized) and expected traffic window(s).
- Sign the attached NDA if needed for logs/trace exchange (attached: nda-summitpay.pdf).

Next meeting: propose 30m on Tue 6/29 or Wed 6/30 to kick off, review access items.

Thanks — Irene
Irene Choi

Katie / Luke — quick operational notes and a recommended minimal pilot commitment to make the financials meaningful:  

Operational checklist (short)- Access: sandbox API key + sample payloads (we need these by Mon 6/28).
- Instrumentation: include token counts per request and separate logs for scoring vs reconciliation so we can split unit economics.
- SRE wrap: we will provide a small client library to integrate KV/prefix caching; ops time is ~2–4 dev days.

Pilot commitment we recommend- Minimum 2-week live window at 5% traffic shadowing OR 1 week at 10% live traffic to capture real tail latency and token distribution. This is to generate statistically significant cost delta.

Measurement & acceptance- We will present a short TCO model showing baseline vs pilot with levers applied (batching, caching, quantized routing).
- Acceptance criteria: cost reduction >=30% OR a clear path to >=30% with identified additional levers; latency must remain within P95 SLA.

I'll own the pilot readout and the cost model fill — Ben will own the workload-class mappings for routing. If you confirm procurement contacts, we can operate in parallel (access + finance).

Marissa Cole
Principal Product Manager, Solutions | Redwood Inference
